title: Wellman Braud leaves; Ripley's 24 hours without repeating a tune
summary: Braud left to open a poolroom; Ripley wrote that the band could play 24 hours without repeating.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x:
Well, what were the circumstances, how
did Wellman Braud leave the band? I read a story once, I wanted
to find out from you if it was true.

I read a story once that somebody had
-- in "Ripley's Believe it or Not." They had in there that
Wellman Braud played the bass, slapped the bass faster than
anybody in the world.
Yeah, and you pronounced his name Breau, right?
Right. And he read this and he came up and after he read that he decided he wanted to be a leader or something like that and then he left the band then. Is that how you remember it?

No. He was tired of traveling. And he wanted to open a business in New York. In fact, he did. A poolroom in New York. And he just told Duke he was tired of traveling, he wanted to stay in New York. Never no argument. Never no big head or nothing.
But Ripley did write that. He wrote that and he said we were the only band that could play 24 hours on a stretch without repeating a tune. He said that. He printed it.
You all had over 24 hours of music you could play without repeating?
We could play 24 hours without repeating a number. Easy! 24 hours. We could play it. Ripley wrote that.
